result.question: Finance wants a number for Transformer 1 at site MAIN. If the gas trend means we'll need corrective oil work soon, how many hours and how much will it cost? Check whether hydrogen, ethylene and acetylene rose between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, give their daily rates in ppm/day, and project each forward 7 days from the last sample. If any projection crosses its IEEE C57.104 Condition 1 limit, treat corrective work as likely within the week. The limits are 100 ppm for hydrogen, 50 ppm for ethylene and 1 ppm for acetylene. Then look through the closed work order history on Transformer 1 for similar corrective jobs, such as oil treatment, degassing, filtration or internal inspection. Give me their average actual hours, average actual cost and average overrun versus plan, and use those to estimate the likely job. If corrective work is likely and no open work order already covers it, draft a work order carrying that estimate in the notes, and give me the MAIN site's overall backlog and overdue counts so I can see what it competes with. If no similar closed work orders exist, say so. In that case, base the estimate on the average of all closed Transformer 1 work orders and label it low-confidence. If none of the gases is projected to cross a limit, don't create a work order. Just report the estimate as a contingency figure.
result.answer:
**Transformer 1 (MAIN) — gas trend, 2024‑01‑15 → 2024‑01‑18 (4 daily samples; no sample on 01‑19)**

| Gas | Readings (ppm) | Rate (least‑squares) | 7‑day projection (2024‑01‑25) | C57.104 Cond. 1 limit | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen | 2845, 2950, 2800, 2900 | +1.5 ppm/day (endpoint +18.3) | ~2,911 ppm | 100 | Already far above; stays above |
| Ethylene | 16684, 16500, 16700, 16600 | −5.2 ppm/day (endpoint −28) | ~16,564 ppm | 50 | Already far above; stays above |
| Acetylene | 7, 6, 8, 7 | +0.2 ppm/day (endpoint 0) | ~8.4 ppm | 1 | Already above; stays above |

Did they rise? Only marginally — hydrogen and acetylene show a slight upward slope within noise; ethylene is flat‑to‑falling. But all three are already well past their Condition 1 limits (ethylene ~330× the limit), and every 7‑day projection remains above the limit → **corrective oil work should be treated as likely within the week.** Note: the numbers don't "cross" the limits during the projection — they're above them from the first sample.

**Closed work order history on Transformer 1**
- Similar corrective jobs (oil treatment / degassing / filtration / internal inspection): **none.**
- Closed work orders of any kind on Transformer 1: **none** (the only WO on this asset is 1000051, open/WAPPR, an OLTC tap‑changer inspection).
- Consequently there is **no historical basis** for average actual hours, average actual cost, or average overrun vs plan — the fallback (average of all closed Transformer 1 WOs) is also empty. Any hours/cost figure for Finance would have to come from a planner or vendor quote; I've labeled it **low‑confidence / TBD** rather than invent one.

**Work order**
- The open WO 1000051 (OLTC inspection) does not cover oil work, so a new corrective WO is warranted. I attempted to draft it (CM, priority 1, notes carrying the DGA evidence and the "no historical estimate — low‑confidence/TBD" statement), but the WO database rejected the write with **403 Forbidden** on both an auto‑numbered and an explicit‑number (1000052) attempt. **No work order was created** — the WO store appears read‑only for this session. If you get write access restored, the draft content above can be re‑submitted as‑is.

**MAIN site backlog it would compete with (full history, 120 months)**
- Backlog (open/non‑terminal): **3** — 1000051 Transformer 1 OLTC inspection (P1, WAPPR), 1000046 Pump 3 bearing wear (P1, APPR), 1000045 Chiller 6 condenser flow anomaly (P2, WAPPR)
- Overdue: **2** (the two 2020 orders with lapsed target dates)
- Completed: 0 (which is why no actuals exist anywhere on the site)

**Bottom line for Finance:** corrective oil work is likely, but there is no defensible hours/cost number from history — it must be quoted, and the WO couldn't be entered because the work order system refused writes.
